title: Function composition
purpose: Describe one transformation whose output becomes the input of another.
meaning: In f composed with g, perform g first and then feed its result to f. Read the written expression from the innermost application outward.

definition.setting: Set-based functions, with an explicitly restricted domain for partial compositions.

signature.composite: A → C when every g output is valid for f

conditions: For a particular x, x must be in dom(g) and g(x) must be in dom(f).
A type checker must establish assignability or require an explicit domain guard; matching scalar-looking numbers is insufficient when their meanings/units differ.
definition.domain_notes: More generally f may have a different declared domain Df; composition is defined on inputs of g whose outputs lie in Df. The simple B match above is a sufficient standard case.

grammar.pronunciation: f composed with g, evaluated at x
grammar.formation_rule: If x is an allowed argument of g and g(x) is an allowed argument of f, form Apply(f, Apply(g, x)).
grammar.precedence: Parenthesized function application; g(x) is a complete operand of f. Composition order differs from ordinary left-to-right prose.

grammar.ast_coverage: The AST models the core right-hand expression, not the complete displayed equality. Output symbols use the explicit output binding map. Do not infer a full formula AST or arbitrary TeX parsing.

scopes.domain_condition: Numeric renderer only: f and g are real polynomial/affine functions; all finite inputs allowed subject to numeric overflow checks.

properties.conditions: Both orders must be defined for comparison.

properties.derivation: Both sides applied to x evaluate to h(f(g(x))). This changes grouping, not order.

prompts.prompt: Before switching order, predict whether the result changes. What would count as evidence?
prompts.answer: Compute both ordered composites at the same input. A difference refutes equality of the two functions; agreement at one input does not prove equality.

prompts.prompt: What must be checked before connecting two transformations?
prompts.answer: The particular inner output must be a valid outer input; for a full typed composition establish the needed domain/type compatibility.
